contentBlocks.text: This week you learned short O, the digraph 'ch', and the blend 'st'. Let's review it all and combine everything into one more sentence!

Quick review: short O sounds like in 'hot' and 'pot' (Day 1). 'ch' is a digraph — two letters, one new sound (Day 2). 'st' is a blend — two letters, both sounds still heard (Day 3). You read two sentences combining these sounds (Day 4). Now read one more sentence combining a word from each: 'Chip can stop the dog.'
Wonderful work these past two weeks! You now know three short vowels, two digraphs, and a consonant blend — real decoding tools you'll use constantly going forward.

objectives: Review short O, the digraph 'ch', and the blend 'st'
Read a new sentence combining words from all three patterns
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child read the new combining sentence independently.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Discuss any uncertain words together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing two full weeks of Grade 1 ELA — three vowels, two digraphs, and a blend!
differentiationTips: Struggling: break the final sentence into smaller word groups before reading it as a whole
Ready for more: ask the child to identify which word in the sentence uses a digraph (Chip) and which uses a blend (stop)
This is a good checkpoint to note which pattern (short O, digraphs, or blends) needs the most re-teaching
teacherGuide.answerKey: The sentence is: 'Chip can stop the dog.' Check that the child reads it accurately and can identify 'Chip' as using the 'ch' digraph and 'stop' as using the 'st' blend.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's short-O, digraph, and blend content into one final combining sentence, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.

generationData.instructions: Trace the sentence, read it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
